messages.subject: geom_tile + coord_map(project="mercator")
parts:
Hi,

First off, thanks to Hadley for ggplot. Its what I have been wanting
in a graphing package for a long,long time. Respect.

I am trying to produce some maps and geom_tile wont work with +
coord_map(project="mercator"). This illustrates my problem:

library(ggplot2)
library(maps)

data = data.frame(lat=c(-41,-42,-41,-42),lon=c(170,170,171,171),var=c
(1,2,3,4))
coast = data.frame(map("nz", plot=FALSE)[c("x","y")])

plot = ggplot(data,aes(x=lon,y=lat,z=NULL)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=var))
+ geom_polygon(data=coast,aes(x=x,y=y))
plot #OK
plot + coord_equal() #OK
plot + coord_map(project="mercator") #Tiles are gone

The only workaround I can think of is to create polygons to represent
each tile and then transform everything, including coastline, to
mercator and then plot of normal coords. Anyone got a better idea?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: geom_tile + coord_map(project="mercator")
parts:
Hi Nick,

That looks like a bug in ggplot2. Unfortunately my hard drive died
last night (luckily everything was backed up), so I don't have
development environment in which to investigate the problem.

However, as you suggested, you can work around the problem by
converting the tiles to explicit polygons:

data <- data.frame(
lat = c(-41,-42,-41,-42),
lon = c(170,170,171,171),
var = c(1,2,3,4)
)
polys <- ddply(data, .(var), function(df)
with(df, rect_to_poly(lon - 0.5, lon + 0.5, lat - 0.5, lat + 0.5))
)

plot <- ggplot(polys, aes(x, y)) +
geom_polygon(data = coast) +
geom_polygon(aes(fill = var, group = var))
plot + coord_map()

ggplot2 should be doing this behind the scenes (as you might guess
from the presence of the rect_to_poly function), and I'm not sure why
it's not. I'll add it to my to do list.

Hadley
